prompt: Create ONE single image, 4:3 aspect ratio: a 2x2 grid of 4 SEPARATE illustrations (2 columns, 2 rows) for a children's picture book, all panels exactly the same size and perfectly aligned, plain white gutters between and around the panels, no frames, no captions, no text, letters or numbers anywhere. Style: Children's picture-book illustration, soft watercolor and gouache with gentle pencil lines, warm golden light, earthy palette (stone beige, olive green, terracotta, deep blue), rounded friendly faces with expressive eyes, the Land of Israel and Babylon in the time of the Mishnah and Talmud (Roman era): stone houses with flat roofs, oil lamps, study halls with low benches and scrolls, markets, olive and carob trees. Jewish sages with beards, tunics and simple robes; women in modest long dresses and head coverings. Calm, warm, safe mood. HEAD COVERING RULE for every panel: every man and every boy (including sons, shepherds, servants, neighbors and children) ALWAYS has his head covered, never bare: a kippah (skullcap) in modern or sages-era scenes, a tallit worn over the head, or in ancient scenes the hood or corner of his robe/cloak drawn over his head or a head-cloth tied with a cord. This overrides any mention of hair in a character description (the hair may show beneath the covering). Women and girls keep their head scarves or coverings as described. Keep every character exactly the same in every panel where they appear: Rabbi Joshua: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Hananiah, a Jewish sage of about 60, short and slightly stout, warm tan skin, twinkling dark eyes, a round friendly face, a full grey-white beard trimmed rounded, a dark-grey cloth cap, a plain earth-brown wool robe over a cream tunic, a leather satchel on a strap across his chest, leather sandals, a simple wooden walking stick; Girl: A bright little girl of about 9, slim, light olive skin, lively hazel eyes, long dark-brown hair in a single braid, a sky-blue long dress with long sleeves and a cream sash, barefoot, stands with hands on hips when she makes a point; Boy: A mischievous little boy of about 7, small and wiry, sun-browned skin, big dark eyes, short messy black curls, a gap-toothed grin, an ochre-yellow knee-length tunic with a brown rope belt, bare feet, often holds a few smooth pebbles. Panels in reading order: 1 BOOK COVER: At a dusty crossroads where a road splits into two paths among olive trees, Rabbi Joshua bends toward the Boy, who sits on a flat stone and points to both roads at once with a cheeky grin. Rabbi Joshua scratches his beard, amused and puzzled. In the distance, a walled town with green gardens on a hill. Warm late-morning light, wide composition with the fork in the road as a clear shape. 2 Inside a study hall with low benches and scrolls, Rabbi Joshua sits on a cushion answering questions, one finger raised and a merry twinkle in his eye. Students and a few richly dressed visitors listen in admiration. Warm light from small high windows and oil lamps. Medium-wide shot, Rabbi Joshua in the center. 3 A wide green field of young wheat under a bright sky, with a thin trodden footpath cutting across it. Rabbi Joshua walks along the path with his stick, pleased to save time. At the edge of the field the Girl stands on the road, calling out to him with one hand raised. Bright morning light, wide shot, the narrow path leading the eye. 4 Rabbi Joshua stands in the middle of the trodden path, laughing heartily with one hand on his belly. The Girl, at the field's edge with hands on hips, smiles a clever smile and points down at the path made by many footprints, and at the bent wheat stalks beside it. Medium shot of the two, golden light, playful mood.
